## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Fix key normalization in `Cache.set` so mixed-case writes are reachable through the case-insensitive lookup.

## Changes

The pull request adds `Cache.set`, raises the default TTL from 60 to 300 seconds, and adds tests for round trips, the default TTL constant, and expiry.

## Critical

(none)

## Important

- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Normalize keys before storing entries — After `set("Alpha", 1)`, `get("Alpha")` returns `None` because `set` stores `"Alpha"` and `get` looks up `"alpha"`. — Callers can miss entries they just wrote, and lookups never reach those entries to remove them after expiry.

## Suggestions

- app/cache.py:7 — comments — Qualify the five-minute TTL as the default — With `Cache(ttl=1)`, entries expire after one second despite the comment “Entries expire 300 seconds after they are written.” The constructor assigns `self._ttl = ttl`, and `set` computes the deadline with `time.monotonic() + self._ttl`. — The comment gives callers the wrong retention period when they supply a custom TTL.
- tests/test_cache.py:18 — tests — Test expiry with the default constructor — If `Cache()` uses a 60-second TTL while `Cache.DEFAULT_TTL` stays at `300`, `test_default_ttl_is_five_minutes` passes because it reads only the constant. — The test would miss a regression that restores one-minute expiry for callers who omit `ttl`. — Fix: Extend `test_default_ttl_is_five_minutes` to exercise `Cache()` with a controlled monotonic clock.
